Yep. Rim protection is a huge asset. Even more important than offensive production imo specifically for big men. See Miami with Hassan. Eliminating pretty much one half of the game which is driving and penetration to the hoop works wonders for a defense. Teams cant go in and out on them because they cant establish the drive thus locking down the perimeter which is a big reason the Heat are 3rd in the league in opposition 3 point % (meaning opponents shoot way lower than average from 3).  Since many of you might be fans Ill give you another example which is pretty much the same in football. Hassan or to a lesser extent Biz is pretty much last years defensive line. If teams cant establish the run than the passing game can be preyed on and neutralized with a somewhat effective secondary. Stephon Gilmore can be compared to Carroll if you want to.  For centers this rim protection is more important than offensive skillset because of how much emphasis there is on the 3 ball and how guard dominated nba scoring is. Unless your Marc Gasol your center being a primary or effective scorer isnt going to give you as much value as rim protection. See Marcin Gortat who is really hurting the Wizards imo even tho he can score effectively.  There are some drawbacks however. Biz plays a huge impact on the defensive end but his lack of a threat offensively can negate his defensive abilities by pretty much making it 4 v 5 on offence. Although when used effectively and say put in screen and roll scenarios with Kyle, Demar, Cojo you can hide this (remember most centers arent there for being a primary scorer) while you cant hide rim protection
